q: Which document is the agreement that fixes the scope of work and the contract amount between the project owner and the constructor?
n: The Owner-Contractor Agreement is the contract proper: it names the parties, the scope and the contract sum. The General Conditions and the Specifications are separate documents bound with it.
ref: UAP Document 301 - General Conditions; SPP Document 202 (2010 SPP, Supplemental IRR of RA 9266) - Regular Design Services

q: Which document describes the design, the materials to be used and the standards of workmanship?
n: The Specifications carry the written technical requirements - materials, workmanship and execution - that the drawings cannot show.
ref: SPP Document 202 (2010 SPP, Supplemental IRR of RA 9266) - Regular Design Services, Sec. 2.4.1 - contract documents

q: Which drawings are submitted to the Office of the Building Official after construction is completed?
n: The application for a Certificate of Occupancy is filed with a notarized Certificate of Completion, the construction logbook and the as-built plans, which record the building as it was actually built.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Sec. 309 - Certificate of Occupancy

q: Which document must be issued before the owner may move into a finished building?
n: No building may be used or occupied until the Building Official issues the Certificate of Occupancy under Sec. 309. The Certificate of Completion is one of its requirements, not a substitute for it.
ref: PD 1096 National Building Code, Revised IRR (2004), Sec. 309 - Certificate of Occupancy

q: What is the maximum imprisonment for a person convicted of violating RA 9266, its IRR or the Code of Ethical Conduct?
n: The penalty is a fine of P100,000 to P5,000,000, or imprisonment of not less than six months but not exceeding six years, or both, at the discretion of the court.
ref: RA 9266 Architecture Act of 2004, Sec. 29 - penal provisions

q: What is the minimum imprisonment for a person convicted of violating RA 9266, its IRR or the Code of Ethical Conduct?
n: The same provision sets the floor at six months and the ceiling at six years, with a fine of P100,000 to P5,000,000 as the alternative.
ref: RA 9266 Architecture Act of 2004, Sec. 29 - penal provisions

q: Which of these is NOT among the architect's responsibilities to the public?
o: Using paid advertisement to promote the services offered
Striving to improve the environment and the life and habitat
Respecting the natural, historic and cultural heritage of the community
Promoting the interest of the professional organization
n: The architect may not use paid advertisement or self-laudatory, exaggerated or misleading publicity. Presenting factual material about the aims and standards of the profession is allowed.
ref: UAP Document 200 - Code of Ethical Conduct, Rule 1-d

q: Which of these is NOT among the architect's responsibilities to the client?
o: Guaranteeing every estimate and cost of the work
Advising the client against a project whose practicability is questionable
Explaining the exact nature and scope of the services from the very beginning
Offering only the services the architect is competent to perform
n: The architect explains the conditional character of estimates and in no case guarantees an estimate or cost, except one submitted as an actual proposal by a contractor.
ref: UAP Document 200 - Code of Ethical Conduct, Rule 2-d

q: Which of these is NOT among the architect's responsibilities to the contractor?
o: Knowingly asking the contractor to correct errors in the contract documents at the contractor's own cost
Furnishing clear, definite and consistent information in the contract documents
Rejecting gifts, commissions and favors from the contractor
Promptly inspecting completed work and issuing the certificate of payment
n: The architect may not knowingly call on the contractor to correct or remedy oversights or errors in the contract documents to the contractor's financial disadvantage - those are the architect's own to fix.
ref: UAP Document 200 - Code of Ethical Conduct, Rule 3-b

q: When is the professional tax receipt (PTR) due each year?
n: The professional tax is payable annually on or before the 31st of January, to the province or city where the professional practises or resides.
ref: RA 7160 Local Government Code, Sec. 139 (d) - professional tax

q: Which permit must be secured first when renewing a business licence?
n: The barangay clearance comes first, because the city or municipality requires it before acting on the mayor's permit. Both are renewed in January, with 20 January the usual deadline.
ref: RA 7160 Local Government Code, Sec. 152 (c) - barangay clearance

q: When is the annual income tax return of an individual due?
n: The return for the preceding calendar year is filed on or before the 15th of April.
ref: NIRC (RA 8424, as amended), Sec. 51 (C) - filing of income tax returns

q: What is the general rate of value-added tax in the Philippines?
n: VAT is 12%, raised from 10% by RA 9337 and effective since February 2006.
ref: NIRC Sec. 106, as amended by RA 9337

q: In comparative selection, what does the client issue to begin the process?
o: An invitation with the terms of reference
n: Comparative selection is run by a committee. It opens with an invitation carrying the terms of reference drawn from the design brief, and the architects respond to that.
ref: SPP Document 201 (2010 SPP) - selection of the architect, comparative selection

q: Who engages and pays the full-time construction supervisor when the owner requires one?
n: Full-time construction supervisors are engaged and paid by the owner. Where there is no project or construction manager, the supervisor works under the technical direction of the architect.
ref: SPP Document 202 (2010 SPP, Supplemental IRR of RA 9266) - Regular Design Services - construction phase services

q: Which method of compensation is described as fair to both parties and flexible and easy to apply?
n: The percentage-based fee on project construction cost is the most common method worldwide, and the one the SPP calls fair to both client and architect and flexible and easy to apply.
ref: SPP Document 210 (2010 SPP) - Methods of Compensation, Sec. 4 - percentage-based fee

q: Which waterproofing is semi-flexible to rigid and is not meant to be left exposed to sunlight and weathering?
n: Cementitious waterproofing is a rigid slurry, cheap and easy to apply, but it has little movement capacity and degrades under UV, so it is used in wet areas and water tanks rather than on exposed decks.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - moisture protection

q: Which waterproofing is a synthetic rubber single-ply flexible membrane?
n: EPDM is a single-ply synthetic rubber sheet, laid loose, ballasted or adhered, and it stays flexible in cold and under UV.
ref: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, 6th ed. - single-ply roof membranes

q: In government infrastructure contracts, what are the liquidated damages for each day the contractor is late?
o: 1/10 of 1% of the cost of the unperformed work
n: Liquidated damages run at least one tenth of one percent of the cost of the unperformed portion for every day of delay. Once they reach 10% of the contract price the procuring entity may rescind the contract.
ref: IRR of RA 12009 (New Government Procurement Act, 2024) - liquidated damages

q: When a material is specified by trade name or catalogue reference, whose approval is needed to substitute another product?
n: Substitutions are approved by the architect, who prepared the specification and judges whether the offered product is equal in quality and performance.
ref: UAP Document 301 - General Conditions, materials and substitutions

q: Which law governs the design of economic and socialized housing?
n: BP 220 sets the lower standards for economic and socialized housing. PD 957 governs ordinary subdivisions and condominiums, which are held to higher standards.
ref: BP 220 (2008 Revised IRR) - economic and socialized housing

q: Which document proves ownership of a parcel of land that has been registered before?
n: A Transfer Certificate of Title is issued each time registered land changes hands. The Original Certificate of Title is the first title, issued when the land is brought under the Torrens system.
ref: PD 1529 Property Registration Decree

q: What does RROW stand for in subdivision planning?
n: The road right of way is the whole strip reserved for the road - carriageway, planting strip and sidewalk - and its minimum width depends on the number of saleable lots.
ref: PD 957 (1981 IRR) and BP 220 (2008 IRR) - road right of way

q: Which SPP document covers the specialized architectural services, the ones formerly called allied services?
n: SPP Document 203 covers specialized architectural services, replacing the 1979 UAP Document 203. SPP 201 is pre-design, SPP 202 regular design services and SPP 205 post-construction services.
ref: SPP Document 203 (2010 SPP, Supplemental IRR of RA 9266) - Specialized Architectural Services

q: Under which provision of RA 9266 is Architectural Interiors a subject in the licensure examination?
n: Sec. 14 lists the subjects for examination. Architectural Interiors sits in group (3), Urban Design and Architectural Interiors, as Part II.
ref: RA 9266 Architecture Act of 2004, Sec. 14 (3) - subjects for examination
